description: §19.7.1 / §18.6 (S474, PERMANENT — security) — the exploit: `@msg = match check("wrong") { .Locked :> "locked", else :> "LOGGED IN" }`. The `else` would take the error variant `.Denied`, so a wrong password would log in. On a failable result `else` covers the success value only; an `else` that would absorb an error variant is E-MATCH-ELSE-ABSORBS-ERROR (and not E-TYPE-020).
provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S474 "⭐ RULED — `else` on a failable match; `scrml fix` S466 readings" item 1 — "an `else` that would absorb errors gets a compile error that names the uncovered error variants" · review:s474-backfill old4 (#1444) `~/.cache/scrml/review/s474-backfill/old4/p1444/m2.scrml`
rationale: §19.7.1 (S474): a plain `_` / `else` arm in a `match` on a failable result covers `.Ok` only; an error variant no arm names makes it E-MATCH-ELSE-ABSORBS-ERROR. `.Denied` is named by no arm here.
